title: Impact of Word Choice Practice 1
description: 4 short texts - 8 focused impact of word choice questions
subject: rla
passage:
TEXT A - Rain Garden

The article says the new soil layer captures runoff before it reaches the street drain.

TEXT B - Repair Delay

The email says a missing part stalled the repair.

TEXT C - Market Crowd

At noon, shoppers packed the narrow aisle.

TEXT D - Research Result

The paper says the new method cuts processing time by about a third.

questions.prompt: Why use captures instead of receives?
questions.explanation: Captures suggests actively taking and holding the runoff.
questions.rule: Use the exact wording and surrounding context as evidence.

options.whyWrong: “To make the article humorous.” does not fit the way the word, phrase, or technique functions in this specific context.
“To prove the soil moves.” describes the opposite effect from the one supported by the passage.

options.text: To show the runoff is illegal.
options.whyWrong: The passage does not provide evidence for the claim “To show the runoff is illegal..” It adds information the text never establishes.

options.text: To emphasize active collection and retention.

questions.prompt: If receives replaced captures, what would be reduced?
questions.explanation: Receives is more neutral and less purposeful.
questions.rule: Use the exact wording and surrounding context as evidence.

options.whyWrong: “the amount of rain” describes the opposite effect from the one supported by the passage.
“the location of the drain” does not fit the way the word, phrase, or technique functions in this specific context.
“the fact soil exists” uses a related idea, but the relationship or conclusion does not match the text.

questions.prompt: How would delayed change the effect?
questions.explanation: Delayed can mean slowed or postponed; stalled suggests a stronger halt.
questions.rule: Use the exact wording and surrounding context as evidence.

It would prove the cause was different.

questions.prompt: If filled replaced packed, what would change?
questions.explanation: Filled indicates occupancy but not the same compression.
questions.rule: Use the exact wording and surrounding context as evidence.

options.whyWrong: “The aisle would become wider.” describes the opposite effect from the one supported by the passage.
“The time would change.” does not fit the way the word, phrase, or technique functions in this specific context.

options.whyWrong: “The shoppers would leave.” uses a related idea, but the relationship or conclusion does not match the text.

questions.prompt: Why use cuts instead of changes?
questions.explanation: Cuts directly communicates reduction and gives the statement force.
questions.rule: Use the exact wording and surrounding context as evidence.
